name: Wyoming
overview: Wyoming issues big game licenses by hunt area and license type through online initial drawings, followed by a leftover drawing and first-come, first-served sales. Preference points are used for resident and nonresident moose and full-price bighorn sheep and for nonresident elk, deer and antelope: 75% of each hunt's licenses go to the applicants with the most points and the remaining 25% to a random drawing of all unsuccessful applicants. Resident elk, deer and antelope, mountain goat, reduced-price and turkey licenses are drawn randomly, and 40% of nonresident elk, deer and antelope licenses are reserved as higher-priced Special licenses with their own drawing.

species.drawSystemSummary: Limited-quota and nonresident region-general elk licenses are drawn. For nonresidents, 75% of each hunt's licenses go to a preference-point drawing (highest points first) and the remaining 25% to a random drawing of all unsuccessful applicants; 40% of nonresident elk licenses are set aside as higher-priced Special licenses drawn separately.
species.residentNote: Residents do not use preference points for elk; resident limited-quota elk licenses are drawn randomly. Resident general elk licenses go on sale over the counter July 16.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents apply Jan. 2 - Feb. 2 for a region general or a limited-quota hunt. Points count only for the first choice and are lost when the first choice is drawn. Party applications use the group's average points (to the 4th decimal). Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).
species.otcSummary: Resident general elk licenses (over the counter from July 16); leftover licenses first come, first served from July 16.

species.drawSystemSummary: Wyoming issues deer licenses (not species-specific unless the hunt limitation says so). Nonresident full-price deer licenses are drawn 75% by preference points and 25% at random; 40% are set aside as Special licenses drawn separately. Resident limited-quota deer licenses are drawn randomly.
species.residentNote: Residents do not use preference points for deer. Resident general deer licenses go on sale over the counter July 16.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents apply for a region general deer license (by region letter) or a limited-quota hunt; region general licenses are valid in any hunt area in the region not totally limited in quota. Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).
species.otcSummary: Resident general deer licenses (over the counter from July 16); leftover licenses first come, first served from July 16.

species.drawSystemSummary: White-tailed-only hunts (e.g. Type 3 any white-tailed deer, Type 8 doe/fawn white-tailed deer) are drawn in the same deer drawing: nonresident full-price licenses 75% by preference points and 25% at random, with a separate Special-license drawing. Reduced-price doe/fawn licenses use no points.
species.residentNote: Residents do not use preference points for deer.
species.nonresidentNote: A second full-price deer license is available only after the initial drawing and only if at least one is a limited-quota Type 3 any white-tailed deer license (leftover drawing or first come, first served). Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).
species.otcSummary: In some hunt areas, after the initial and leftover drawings, unlimited reduced-price doe/fawn white-tailed deer licenses may be purchased.

species.residentNote: Residents do not use preference points for antelope.
species.nonresidentNote: In the initial drawing an applicant may apply for one full-price and up to two reduced-price doe/fawn antelope licenses. species.drawSystemSummary: Resident and nonresident moose licenses are drawn 75% by preference points and 25% at random. An applicant may list only one hunt area choice. Licenses are allocated 90% resident / 10% nonresident by statute.
species.residentNote: Type 1 moose is once in a lifetime; a successful Type 4 applicant must wait five years to apply again or buy a point.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents must elect a preference point when applying; unsuccessful applicants who elected it have the $150 point fee deducted from the refund. Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).

species.drawSystemSummary: Full-price (Type 1/2) bighorn sheep licenses are drawn 75% by preference points and 25% at random for residents and nonresidents, with one hunt area choice. Reduced-price Type 6/7 ewe/lamb licenses are drawn without points. Licenses are allocated 90% resident / 10% nonresident by statute.
species.residentNote: A Type 1 or Type 2 bighorn sheep license is once in a lifetime (applicants who drew after 2017 may not apply again).
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents must elect a preference point when applying; the $150 point fee is deducted from the refund if unsuccessful. Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).

species.residentNote: Type 1 or Type 2 is once in a lifetime (no reapplying if drawn after 1995); since 2019 prior Type 1/2 holders may apply for Type A licenses.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).

species.drawSystemSummary: Spring and fall wild turkey licenses (for 2026 fall / 2027 spring: Area 1 general and Area 1 Type 3 limited quota) are applied for in separate spring and fall drawings without preference points. One spring and one fall license per person in the initial drawing.
species.residentNote: After the initial drawing a person may receive up to three turkey licenses per season, provided at least two are limited-quota Type 3 licenses.
species.otcSummary: Additional licenses after the initial drawing as allowed by Chapter 20; see the WGFD turkey regulation.

species.drawSystemSummary: Black bear licenses are not part of the WGFD drawings (no draw application or odds are published). Each hunt area or group of areas closes when its female mortality limit is reached, otherwise on the regulation's closing date; spring overages are subtracted from the fall limit.
species.residentNote: Hunters must confirm an area is open (closure hotline 1-800-264-1280). Bait sites are registered separately.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).
species.otcSummary: Resident black bear license $47; nonresident $373 (2026 fee list). No drawing.

species.drawSystemSummary: Mountain lion licenses are not part of the WGFD drawings. Each hunt area closes when its mortality limit is reached (separate resident and nonresident limits in designated areas), otherwise on the regulation's closing date. A person may hold one full-price and one reduced-price lion license per calendar year.
species.residentNote: Reduced-price licenses are valid only in designated hunt areas and require a current full-price license.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents may not hunt big or trophy game in designated wilderness areas unless accompanied by a licensed professional guide or a resident guide (one guide per two nonresident hunters).
species.otcSummary: Resident mountain lion license $32 (reduced price $20); nonresident $373 (reduced price $92). No drawing.
